title: How to use the `coi` library
text: coi package small tool calculate metrics terrestrial laser scanning (TLS) point clouds. name coi stands “crown overlap index” one metrics can extracted package. COI calculated described Täuber et al. (prep.) inspired earlier index called crown complementarity index (CCI), presented Williams et al. (2017). CCI can also calculated coi package. Finally package can also extract box dimension, structural complexity metric described Seidel (2018).

title: How to use the `coi` library
text: point cloud operations coi use pt_cld class — lightweight S3 wrapper around 3-column numeric matrix columns x, y, z. can create one data.frame, matrix, individual vectors: package functions require pt_cld objects input produce clear errors pass plain matrix data.frame instead.
code: library(coi)  # From a data.frame (e.g. as returned by rlas::read.las()) df <- data.frame(x = runif(100), y = runif(100), z = runif(100)) cloud <- as_pt_cld(df) cloud #> pt_cld with 100 points #>   x: [0.007, 0.997] #>   y: [0.004, 1] #>   z: [0.017, 0.984]  # Access coordinates head(cloud$x) #> [1] 0.080750138 0.834333037 0.600760886 0.157208442 0.007399441 0.466393497

title: How to use the `coi` library
text: First attach library generate two artificial point clouds spheres radius 1 m voxel resolution 0.01 m centers 0.5 m distance x-axis. Next, voxelize point clouds common resolution. artificial spheres already voxel resolution. work real-world TLS data resolution variable across point cloud. algorithms produce meaningful data need voxelised cloud. can now take look two voxelised spheres.  Now extract interaction point cloud spheres using extract_interaction function. need define d_max. choose 0.1 m. can add interaction cloud plot. returns = "cloud" argument ensures value function point cloud can use plotting.  interaction cloud, chosen d_max total size interacting clouds, can now calculate COI using compute_coi function. However compute_coi don’t need entire interaction cloud, just 1-D vector individual points’ distances. re-run extract_interaction returns = "distances".
code: library(ggplot2)  sphere1 <- gen_sphere(   r = 0.5,   res = 0.01,   center = c(-0.2, 0, 0) ) sphere2 <- gen_sphere(   r = 0.5,   res = 0.01,   center = c(0.2, 0, 0) ) sphere1_v <- voxelize(   cloud = sphere1,   res = 0.05 ) sphere2_v <- voxelize(   cloud = sphere2,   res = 0.05 )  spheres <- ggplot() +   theme_void() +   geom_point(     data = as.data.frame(sphere1_v),     aes(x, y),     size = 3,     color = "black",     alpha = 0.03   ) +   geom_point(     data = as.data.frame(sphere2_v),     aes(x, y),     size = 3,     color = "red",     alpha = 0.03   ) spheres d_max <- 0.1  interaction_cloud <- extract_interaction(   cloud_i = sphere1_v,   cloud_j = sphere2_v,   d_max = d_max,   returns = "cloud" )  spheres +   geom_point(     data = as.data.frame(interaction_cloud),     aes(x, y),     size = 3,     color = "green",     alpha = 0.03   ) interaction_distances <- extract_interaction(   cloud_i = sphere1_v,   cloud_j = sphere2_v,   d_max = d_max,   returns = "distances" )  total_size <- nrow(sphere1_v) + nrow(sphere2_v)  compute_coi(   distances = interaction_distances,   size_weight = total_size,   d_max = d_max ) #> [1] 0.5111444

title: How to use the `coi` library
text: entire process useful first want test different values vox_res d_max, inspect interaction clouds running whole pipeline data. However found suitable values can skip use simple coi function one step.
code: coi(   cloud_i = sphere1,   cloud_j = sphere2,   d_max = d_max,   vox_res = 0.05 ) #> [1] 0.5111444

text: CCI investigate two point clouds interact. need two spheres . create two pairs spheres b demonstrate cci reacts volume differences interacting clouds. spheres radius 2 m. b one r 2 m 3 m. CCI currently exists --one function cci, makes calculation super easy. just need size vertical strata type hull layer. Usually concave hulls exact natural contexts (though sometimes problems). since look spheres convex hulls totally fine. resulting values see cci = 0 two clouds exactly homogenous vertical layer, b much higher cci.
code: sphere1_a <- gen_sphere(   r = 2,   res = 0.05,   center = c(0, 0, 0) ) sphere2_a <- gen_sphere(   r = 2,   res = 0.05,   center = c(0, 0, 0) )  sphere1_b <- gen_sphere(   r = 2,   res = 0.05,   center = c(0, 0, 0) ) sphere2_b <- gen_sphere(   r = 3,   res = 0.05,   center = c(0, 0, 0) ) cci(   cloud_i = sphere1_a,   cloud_j = sphere2_a,   strata_size = 0.2,   hull_type = "convex",   vox_res = 0.1 ) #> [1] 0 cci(   cloud_i = sphere1_b,   cloud_j = sphere2_b,   strata_size = 0.2,   hull_type = "convex",   vox_res = 0.1 ) #> [1] 0.5347726

title: How to use the `coi` library
text: Finally can extract box dimension described Seidel (2018). use two spheres differing sizes. However, simple geometric shapes like sphere Box dimension always produce higher values larger shapes points. real magic parameter shines natural fractal shapes like trees.
code: sphere_a <- gen_sphere(   r = 0.5,   res = 0.05 ) sphere_b <- gen_sphere(   r = 1,   res = 0.05 )  threshold <- 0.1  boxdim(   cloud = sphere_a,   threshold = threshold,   vox_res = NULL,   warnings = FALSE ) #> [1] 2.272419 boxdim(   cloud = sphere_b,   threshold = threshold,   vox_res = NULL,   warnings = FALSE ) #> [1] 2.367149

what: Extract Tree-Tree Interaction Metrics from TLS Point Clouds
title: Extract Tree-Tree Interaction Metrics from TLS Point Clouds
text: coi small library can extract three metrics relevant physical tree-tree interactions point clouds representing trees. Namely crown overlap index (COI), gives package name described Täuber et al. (2026) crown complementarity index (CCI) described Williams et al. (2017). box dimension structural complexity described Seidel (2018).
